--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Labeling the timely allow as a denial is wrong. An allow proceeds through normal collision and confirmation. Labeling the timely deny as a policy refusal is correct. Labeling the reservation failure as a denial is wrong. It is the proposed `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, with admission-fault cleanup and the `INTERNAL_ERROR` reconnect disposition. The reservation failure is the outcome that invokes no provider.

Document support:
QUOTE: "| Timely identity result | Allow follows normal collision and confirmation rules; deny remains a policy refusal |"
QUOTE: "At capacity, refuse before provider invocation and report proposed `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, not `IDENTITY_REJECTED` or a per-route `POLICY` denial."
QUOTE: "Its terminal effects follow the existing admission-fault cleanup and `INTERNAL_ERROR` reconnect disposition, but do not misreport a provider fault when no provider was called."

Inference or gap: NONE

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: P may be released now because its invocation permit was revoked before invocation. Q must retain its reservation despite cancellation until its evaluation settles and AGP disposes the retained work. R must retain its reservation until its owned result is disposed; settlement alone is insufficient. If disposal is performed at this checkpoint, R can then be released exactly once.

Document support:

QUOTE: "A reservation whose invocation permit is revoked before the provider is called can be released immediately."
QUOTE: "Its capacity remains reserved while that result is waiting, preventing an unbounded queue of settled results behind the executor."
QUOTE: "On eventual provider settlement, dispose the retained work and release its reservation exactly once; stale success and stale failure have the same lack of authority."

Inference or gap: NONE.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Neither the prepared identity result nor the queued stop completion may proceed as an ordinary transaction after numeric terminal replacement. The node owns the runtime gate and serialized coordinator. Exhaustion from any publication closes that gate, sets host authority to Failed, invalidates admission and other action permits, and discards the exhausting ordinary plan. The prepared identity result loses effect authority. The stop continuation must observe the same gate and cannot overwrite Failed, publish another revision, or rearm an adjacency. OperationsStore cannot independently terminalize only the projection.

Document support:

QUOTE: "All runtime operations publications must reach this coordinator, including ones outside admission, so an unrelated counter/event/revision exhaustion revokes admission and acquisition authority too."
QUOTE: "Close the runtime gate and set host authority to `Failed`; invalidate the node generation, all admission invocation/result permits, acquisition adoption permits, supervisor wait/timer generations, and outstanding ordinary action intents."
QUOTE: "A stop or listener-failure continuation already queued must observe the terminal gate and must not overwrite `Failed` with `Stopping` or `Stopped`, generate another revision, or rearm an adjacency."

Inference or gap: NONE.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: The old rejection cannot fault the replacement or release the replacement's reservation. Application checks the runtime gate, controller identity/incarnation, admission kind, exact token and deadline. The removed controller's completion is stale regardless of the shared peer identity or the replacement's timeliness. Its bounded accounting owner observes and disposes the old completion and releases only the old evaluation's reservation once settlement and disposal permit. It cannot introduce a new session fault or expiry.

Document support:

QUOTE: "Route the prepared completion through a short executor turn that checks the runtime authority gate, controller identity, admission kind, token and deadline;"
QUOTE: "Runtime authority revoked, controller replaced, admission kind/token stale, or another terminal cause already committed | Dispose the retained completion through its bounded owner; no admission event, identity effect, route effect or new terminal cause"
QUOTE: "Revocation detaches the result's session-effect target; a late observer retains only bounded work-accounting state, not a closure that keeps the controller and channel alive."

Inference or gap: NONE.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Nothing may start. When backoff expires with route capacity still full, only the timer is consumed and one waiter is kept or registered. No new attempt begins and `retryAt` is cleared. The later notification carries no permit. The start-turn level check finds the slot taken, so the waiter remains with the current capacity reason. The remembered route-refusing pool persists until an actual next acquisition begins. Identity availability is also checked at start.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Consume only the timer; retain/register one waiter and the ended attempt projection"
QUOTE: "The start-turn level check keeps the waiter; an older notification carries no permit"
QUOTE: "Immediately before local acquisition, check identity-pool availability and any pool that caused that adjacency's prior local capacity refusal."
QUOTE: "Remembered refusing pools persist across capacity fluctuations and backoff until one actual next acquisition begins; they are then consumed, not inherited indefinitely."
QUOTE: "Availability is not a reservation, and provider invocation still reserves atomically."

Inference or gap: NONE

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: The malformed/incomplete result fails preparation. It cannot consume the route revision, mutate routing, or authorize an ACK. The design's admission-fault model supports treating an invalid current result as a session fault, but it does not explicitly define the invalid-route-result-to-terminal transition. The complete valid result denying one tuple is explicitly nonfatal: policy denial is an ordinary route outcome, and a successfully prepared, guarded and committed proposal consumes one revision and authorizes one ACK. Reserved evaluation capacity does not validate either result.

Document support:

QUOTE: "Validate the result against exactly that subset, including an empty subset."
QUOTE: "Neither the controller revision nor routing state may change until that complete preparation succeeds."
QUOTE: "Success, rejection, thrown/invalid result and timer callbacks obey the same exact current-token guard"
QUOTE: "Complete valid allow/deny decisions cause one atomic revision/RIB change and one ACK; per-route denials remain nonfatal"

Inference or gap: Session termination for malformed results is a reasonable admission-fault interpretation, not a fully specified transition in this document. Its exact event/disposition is missing; nonfatal policy denial and the malformed proposal's lack of commit authority are explicit.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Equality counts as expired. The route result plan and its unconsumed ordinary permit are discarded, with no route, revision or ACK effects. In the same serialized turn, the session controller's single expiry decision path prepares and preflights `AdmissionExpired`. It then commits it through the node coordinator, without waiting for the timer. This route expiry uses the Established expiry actions: invalidate the continuation, send `INTERNAL_ERROR` only if safe, purge and release. Result authority is revoked, the timer is cancelled and teardown starts. The already settled result's reservation is released only when that result is disposed.

Document support:
QUOTE: "a result is timely only while `now < deadline`."
QUOTE: "Equality is expired, and provider settlement time does not replace the final application-time check."
QUOTE: "| A bound expires between preparation and the final guard | Discard the unconsumed ordinary permit and result plan; prepare and preflight the expiry transition in the same turn, with no result effects |"
QUOTE: "The session controller owns the serialized transition; timer delivery and result application call the same expiry decision path, not separate terminal owners."
QUOTE: "select `AdmissionExpired` unless the identity/OPEN precedence below selects `OpenExpired`; do not wait for the scheduled timer input"
QUOTE: "Route expiry retains the Established expiry actions: invalidate the continuation, send `INTERNAL_ERROR` only if safe, purge and release."

Inference or gap: The phrase "a bound expires between preparation and the final guard" is read here to include the case where the final guard observes equality. That reading follows from the `now < deadline` rule.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: The complete valid list with one policy denial is a normal outcome. The denial is nonfatal, and the result yields one atomic revision/RIB change and one ACK. The malformed or incomplete list is rejected without retaining an unbounded copy. It causes no revision, RIB change or ACK, and leaves no partial routing state. Whether the malformed list ends the session is only inferred: it appears to be an admission fault with the existing fault cleanup and `INTERNAL_ERROR` disposition.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Complete valid allow/deny decisions cause one atomic revision/RIB change and one ACK; per-route denials remain nonfatal"
QUOTE: "reject invalid shape without retaining an unbounded copy"
QUOTE: "a failed preparation leaves no partial routing state"
QUOTE: "Success, rejection, thrown/invalid result and timer callbacks obey the same exact current-token guard"

Inference or gap: The design does not explicitly classify an invalid route result as a session-terminal admission fault. That classification rests on the existing contract, which is not reproduced here.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: When both deadlines have elapsed, admission authority has expired and must not commit a result. However, the document does not resolve an equal-deadline tie between OPEN expiry and identity-admission expiry, or identify which terminal transition wins independently of delivery order. Delivery of the admission callback first is not a documented tie-breaking rule. In the separate early-wake observation, no deadline-expiry transition is justified by that wake: neither deadline is elapsed. A current timer generation does not itself establish expiry.

Document support:

QUOTE: "Independent provider budget, consistent with the present default OPEN budget; the earlier applicable OPEN deadline still wins"
QUOTE: "Use monotonic elapsed time, tokened timer generations and deadline checks at invocation and commit."
QUOTE: "The reducer also rejects mismatched admission fault and expiry tokens as defence in depth."

Inference or gap: Equal-deadline priority is missing. No explicit early-callback rearming transition is supplied; refusing premature expiry follows the monotonic-deadline requirement, but the precise rescheduling action is unspecified.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Not permitted. Result normalization (property access, cloning, provider-controlled callbacks) must happen outside the executor. It produces bounded, owned, immutable data before the short guarded executor turn. Abort-event delivery must also stay outside the executor, and is requested only after authority has been revoked or detached. Both can run application code. The serialized prepare-to-install sequence forbids external callbacks between preparation and installation.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Normalize a potentially current provider result outside the executor into bounded owned immutable data"
QUOTE: "Property access, cloning and provider-controlled callbacks must not become application code running inside the executor."
QUOTE: "Provider calls and abort-event delivery both stay outside the executor because either can run application code."
QUOTE: "without yielding, recursive publication or external callbacks between preparation and installation"

Inference or gap: NONE

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Not permitted. Normalizing the result and delivering the abort event can both run provider or application code, so both must happen outside the executor. Normalization happens before the completion is routed into the short serialized turn. That turn only checks authority and installs the already prepared owned data. Cooperative cancellation is requested outside the executor, after authority has been revoked synchronously.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Normalize a potentially current provider result outside the executor into bounded owned immutable data; reject invalid shape without retaining an unbounded copy. Property access, cloning and provider-controlled callbacks must not become application code running inside the executor."
QUOTE: "Provider calls and abort-event delivery both stay outside the executor because either can run application code."
QUOTE: "Once expiry commits, revoke result authority, cancel the timer and detach the effect target synchronously; request cooperative cancellation outside the executor and start the owned teardown."

Inference or gap: NONE

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Detachment cannot justify restarting D or dropping the active cleanup deadline. The existing cleanup work is transferred to a bounded owner, and the single budget began with the committed cause. The later write timeout cannot replace that already-winning session cause or authorize a second session terminal disposition. Numeric failure separately closes node authority and creates its terminal capture. Until terminal evidence is consumed, cleanup must continue under the retained budget; detached cleanup cannot publish ordinary operations changes.

Document support:

QUOTE: "Start one teardown budget when the terminal cause commits."
QUOTE: "transfer still-needed reader/channel cleanup to its existing bounded cleanup owner."
QUOTE: "Fatal notification, invalid input, transport rejection or terminal | Bypass the barrier and use the one terminal disposition; preserve already-observed FIFO transport evidence"
QUOTE: "These tasks cannot restore live authority, schedule retry or publish operations changes, even if they settle immediately."

Inference or gap: Preserving D across ownership transfer follows the one-budget requirement. The document does not detail the transferred timer/guard representation or a write-timeout-specific cause-precedence transition; it does require one winning session disposition and continued bounded cleanup.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: The projection is not necessarily wrong. A never-attempted adjacency blocked on identity capacity is `retry-wait` with a capacity reason, no `retryAt` and no `activeControllerId`. Disabled reconnect does not prevent the initial attempt or its capacity wait. Waiting consumes no attempt and represents no timer. Only identity capacity must open, because there is no remembered route refusal and route pressure alone does not block an identity-only phase. Inference: the reason should be `identity-admission-capacity`, not the combined value.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Register one waiter; no attempt, session token or backoff is manufactured"
QUOTE: "`retry-wait`, capacity reason, no `retryAt`, no `activeControllerId`; `retryAttempt` unchanged"
QUOTE: "`reconnect.enabled = false` prevents repeat attempts, not the initial configured attempt or its pre-acquisition capacity wait."
QUOTE: "At eligibility checks, identity capacity is always required; route capacity is required only when that set includes a local route-capacity refusal."
QUOTE: "Route-pool pressure alone does not prohibit an unrelated identity-only phase"
QUOTE: "`retryAt` is the wall-time projection recorded when a real monotonic backoff timer is armed, not an estimate of when capacity will become available."

Inference or gap: The choice of the identity-only reason when the route pool is also full is inferred from the eligibility rule.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: No. The recommended API is one shared, optional second parameter that AGP always supplies. One-argument providers may ignore it and still type-check. There is no split between CLI and browser interfaces. Cancellation enters only through process-local `AdmissionEvaluationOptions { signal }`. The request/result DTOs and their schemas stay unchanged. Even if a provider ignores the signal, the work ledger still applies.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Recommendation: add one shared process-local `AdmissionEvaluationOptions` with a `signal` capability as an optional second parameter to both ports' `evaluate` methods."
QUOTE: "AGP always supplies it; existing one-argument implementations may ignore it."
QUOTE: "Keep the request and result DTOs unchanged and credential-free, and keep clocks, callback handles and cancellation authority out of their schemas."
QUOTE: "| Compatibility | Current providers still type-check; new options remain process-local; no protocol-schema change or browser/CLI policy split |"

Inference or gap: This is a recommendation that has not been adopted. Provider inventory and compile checks are still required.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: No. The recommendation adds an optional second parameter, which one-argument providers may ignore. It requires no browser/CLI split. Cancellation enters through a process-local `AdmissionEvaluationOptions.signal` that AGP always passes as the second `evaluate` argument. Request/result DTOs stay unchanged, with cancellation authority kept out of their schemas. This is a recommendation pending public type/export review and compatibility checks.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Recommendation: add one shared process-local `AdmissionEvaluationOptions` with a `signal` capability as an optional second parameter to both ports' `evaluate` methods."
QUOTE: "AGP always supplies it; existing one-argument implementations may ignore it."
QUOTE: "Keep the request and result DTOs unchanged and credential-free, and keep clocks, callback handles and cancellation authority out of their schemas."
QUOTE: "Current providers still type-check; new options remain process-local; no protocol-schema change or browser/CLI policy split"
QUOTE: "Status: proposed behavior, not adopted or implemented."

Inference or gap: NONE

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: The design does not authorize skipping. Its sequence invokes after a committed reservation, and it explicitly requires validating against "an empty subset". That implies an empty-subset invocation is a legitimate case. A skip optimization is neither explicitly forbidden nor allowed. If the provider is invoked, the only valid decision list is empty: exactly one decision per requested tuple, and none were requested.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Validate the result against exactly that subset, including an empty subset."
QUOTE: "the contract requires policy decisions only for routes not already statically rejected"
QUOTE: "returns exactly one decision per requested tuple"

Inference or gap: Missing rule on whether a zero-eligible snapshot may bypass the provider. If it may, the design also does not say what happens to the already-committed reservation in that case.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Starting the new route admission stops the drain until its result arrives. The new ordinary ACK joins the same FIFO and cannot bypass older commands or obtain early protocol effects. The head's queue reservation stays in place while synchronous dispatch prepares the command. It may be removed only after that dispatch has disposed the input or transferred it to another bounded owner, here the reserved evaluation record. It need not remain in the queue until provider settlement once that ownership transfer is complete.

Document support:

QUOTE: "processing a queued command that starts another admission stops that drain until the new result arrives."
QUOTE: "New ordinary arrivals join the same FIFO throughout; terminal commands still bypass it."
QUOTE: "Dequeue only after dispatch has disposed the input or transferred it to another bounded owner, including a reserved evaluation record when another admission starts."

Inference or gap: NONE.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: No. Identity success does not remove the opening bound. The OPEN timer keeps its separate authority through confirmation, even when hold is zero. Once that deadline has elapsed, the existing OPEN expiry applies. The bound ends normally only when the session reaches `Established`, or otherwise at teardown.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Preserve the outer opening deadline through `OpenConfirm`, including when negotiated hold is zero"
QUOTE: "after identity commit, the still-active OPEN timer retains its separate authority through confirmation."
QUOTE: "The OPEN timer remains armed until `Established` or teardown; admission success cannot leave an unlimited confirmation phase when hold is zero."

Inference or gap: The design names `OpenExpired` only in the identity-evaluation context. Using it as the transition in OpenConfirm is inferred from the existing OPEN timer authority.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: P may be released immediately: its invocation permit was revoked before any evaluation began. Q must remain reserved despite cancellation; release requires actual settlement and disposal of its retained work. R must also remain reserved at this checkpoint, because settlement alone is insufficient while its owned result awaits disposal. R can be released when that disposal occurs. Each release happens exactly once.

Document support:

QUOTE: "A reservation whose invocation permit is revoked before the provider is called can be released immediately."
QUOTE: "Its capacity remains reserved while that result is waiting, preventing an unbounded queue of settled results behind the executor."
QUOTE: "On eventual provider settlement, dispose the retained work and release its reservation exactly once; stale success and stale failure have the same lack of authority."

Inference or gap: NONE.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Neither claim is established. The document provides no certification of 500 simultaneous browser peers, workload measurements, or browser physical-release guarantee. The defaults are review recommendations, with identity evaluation count derived from maxPendingHandshakes and route evaluation count from maxSessions; they are not independently measured deployment capacities. Counts bound outstanding AGP evaluations, including revoked unfinished work and retained results. Protocol/schema limits bound retained logical inputs per call. Neither bounds arbitrary provider allocations, hidden descendant tasks, physical JavaScript heap usage, or CPU execution.

Document support:

QUOTE: "These defaults are recommendations for review, not existing runtime behaviour or workload measurements."
QUOTE: "Proposed `maxIdentityAdmissionEvaluations` | Resolved `maxPendingHandshakes`"
QUOTE: "Proposed `maxRouteAdmissionEvaluations` | Resolved `maxSessions`"
QUOTE: "The request's protocol/schema limits bound the retained logical input size per call; these counts do not claim to bound a provider's arbitrary allocations or physical JavaScript heap bytes."
QUOTE: "No in-process acceptance claim includes stopping synchronous infinite computation, proving arbitrary provider allocations freed, or proving browser-native cleanup."

Inference or gap: NONE. A concrete peer-count certification would require evidence beyond this design.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Both queries return the same terminal capture: the captured evaluation count still includes the two unfinished reservations, all other values remain as captured, the revision remains the terminal revision, and capturedAt remains T. Private late settlement/disposal may free internal reservations but cannot update public counters, events or revision. The count is historical last-known accounting at T, not evidence that those resources remain physically allocated at query time, nor proof that all physical resources were ever released.

Document support:

QUOTE: "Freeze its resource values, revision and `capturedAt` together; subsequent aggregate and focused queries return that same terminal capture, not a new timestamp on old counts."
QUOTE: "later private disposal can release internal reservations but cannot publish a new revision, event or counter."
QUOTE: "The final count is last-known at the terminal capture, not a live promise that resources remain allocated or that cleanup has finished."

Inference or gap: NONE.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Detachment preserves D or may force cleanup sooner; it cannot restart the deadline or disable its guard while terminal observation is pending. Numeric failure closes ordinary authority, but the transferred cleanup owner retains exact cleanup-generation authority and the original deadline. The later write timeout may force an earlier channel abort, but cannot replace the committed protocol cause, publish another teardown event or restart the budget. The sole reader still consumes terminal evidence; detached cleanup cannot publish operations or schedule retry.

Document support:

QUOTE: "Node stop/failure overtakes an existing controller cleanup | Preserve its deadline or force cleanup sooner, never restart it; detached cleanup may run after the ordinary runtime gate closes"
QUOTE: "After numeric terminal replacement, its exact cleanup-generation checks remain usable, but cleanup cannot publish operations, schedule retry or restore a controller."
QUOTE: "Per-send timeout expires after a terminal cause has committed | It may force channel abort earlier, but cannot replace the cause, publish another teardown event or restart the teardown budget"

Inference or gap: NONE.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Revoke the pending admission's authority and discard the queued semantic commands, releasing continuation reservations as their retained inputs are disposed. Neither the data command nor the credit-bearing command receives its ordinary protocol effect; credit cannot be applied early. The invoked, unsettled provider's evaluation reservation remains occupied despite cancellation. The sole reader must still consume already-accepted transport FIFO evidence through the ordered terminal record, draining without protocol effects after logical release. Queue disposal is not transport drain, provider settlement, or proof of native release.

Document support:

QUOTE: "On expiry or terminal disposition, revoke authority first, cancel its timer, detach its effect target and request cooperative cancellation outside the executor"
QUOTE: "Reading ahead is not permission to apply a queued packet's peer-credit grant early."
QUOTE: "An admitted packet may become semantically inert after a session-fatal event, but the transport's already-accepted FIFO must still be drained"
QUOTE: "Both current and revoked-but-unsettled work consume their pool; neither timeout, connection replacement nor snapshot removal returns a slot."

Inference or gap: Releasing continuation storage follows actual input disposal and ownership conservation; it does not release the distinct evaluation or transport reservations prematurely.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: The projection is valid for initial capacity waiting even with reconnect disabled. It represents neither a consumed attempt nor a real retry timer; no attempt, session token, active controller or retryAt need exist. Identity capacity must become available for this initial identity-only acquisition. The unrelated full route pool does not block it because there is no prior local route-capacity refusal. Actual start still requires all ordinary eligibility guards, and later admission reservation remains atomic rather than guaranteed by the capacity observation.

Document support:

QUOTE: "Initial acquisition eligible, identity pool full | Register one waiter; no attempt, session token or backoff is manufactured"
QUOTE: "`reconnect.enabled = false` prevents repeat attempts, not the initial configured attempt or its pre-acquisition capacity wait."
QUOTE: "Route-pool pressure alone does not prohibit an unrelated identity-only phase; a route-capacity refusal parks that affected adjacency on route capacity as well."

Inference or gap: NONE.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: P may be released now, because its provider was never invoked. Q stays reserved while its provider is pending. Cancellation does not release it. Q is released once, only after its evaluation settles and AGP disposes the retained request/result. R has settled, but settlement alone releases nothing. Its slot stays reserved until AGP disposes the owned result. R may be released at this checkpoint only if that disposal actually happens here.

Document support:
QUOTE: "A reservation whose invocation permit is revoked before the provider is called can be released immediately."
QUOTE: "After invocation, no reset merely because the session ended or the abort signal fired"
QUOTE: "Its capacity remains reserved while that result is waiting, preventing an unbounded queue of settled results behind the executor."
QUOTE: "Release a provider-work reservation only on the existing uninvoked-permit or settlement-plus-disposal condition, even when this result path discovered expiry."

Inference or gap: The design does not say exactly when a settled result counts as disposed during cleanup. It only requires that disposal has actually happened before the release.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Nothing may start. When backoff expires, only the timer is consumed, and one waiter is kept along with the projection of the ended attempt. The release notification carries no permit. The serialized start check sees the route pool full again and keeps the waiter, with no attempt, no increment and no `retryAt`. The remembered refusing-pool set (route) persists until an actual next acquisition begins. Identity capacity is also always required.

Document support:
QUOTE: "| Backoff expires but capacity is still unavailable | Consume only the timer; retain/register one waiter and the ended attempt projection | `retry-wait`, capacity reason, no `retryAt`; no new attempt |"
QUOTE: "| Capacity opens and is used elsewhere before this adjacency starts | The start-turn level check keeps the waiter; an older notification carries no permit | `retry-wait`, current capacity reason; retain a still-live timer only |"
QUOTE: "Remembered refusing pools persist across capacity fluctuations and backoff until one actual next acquisition begins; they are then consumed, not inherited indefinitely."
QUOTE: "Capacity wakes neither increment reconnect attempts nor restart an already-running backoff, and stop removes all wait records."

Inference or gap: NONE

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: No to both. Draining stops at the head that started the new admission, until that result arrives. The new ordinary route ACK joins the same FIFO behind the backlog and cannot bypass it; only terminal commands bypass. The head's queue reservation is removed (dequeued) only in the dispatch turn that transfers the input to the reserved evaluation record of the new admission. Until then the head stays reserved in place, without being moved to a separate task queue.

Document support:
QUOTE: "processing a queued command that starts another admission stops that drain until the new result arrives."
QUOTE: "New ordinary arrivals join the same FIFO throughout; terminal commands still bypass it."
QUOTE: "Use the queue's head without releasing its reservation while the synchronous dispatch turn prepares the command; do not dequeue into a separate task queue."
QUOTE: "Dequeue only after dispatch has disposed the input or transferred it to another bounded owner, including a reserved evaluation record when another admission starts."

Inference or gap: NONE

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Labeling the timely identity allow as policy denial is wrong: it follows normal collision and confirmation rules, without promising that it must ultimately become established. Labeling the timely current identity deny as policy refusal is correct. Labeling local evaluation-slot exhaustion as identity policy denial is wrong: report AdmissionCapacityExceeded with the exact current admission kind/token and existing admission-fault cleanup/INTERNAL_ERROR reconnect disposition. Capacity refusal invokes no provider; it must not be represented as IDENTITY_REJECTED or a provider fault.

Document support:

QUOTE: "Timely identity result | Allow follows normal collision and confirmation rules; deny remains a policy refusal"
QUOTE: "At capacity, refuse before provider invocation and report proposed `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, not `IDENTITY_REJECTED` or a per-route `POLICY` denial."
QUOTE: "Its terminal effects follow the existing admission-fault cleanup and `INTERNAL_ERROR` reconnect disposition, but do not misreport a provider fault when no provider was called."

Inference or gap: NONE.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Adopting an exact winner that is already Established applies the successful reset once, for that success. The older loser's later success callback is stale and cannot reset newer history. Cancelling a dial timer for a winner still in OpenConfirm only removes scheduling authority. It preserves the accumulated failure history, because no establishment success has occurred.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Exact current winner enters `Established`, or an already-established exact winner is adopted"
QUOTE: "Confirm current winner/incarnation, apply the successful reset once for that success, and keep dial suppression; stale or duplicate success notifications cannot reset newer history"
QUOTE: "Clearing a retry timer because a winner suppresses dialing removes its scheduling authority, not accumulated failure history."
QUOTE: "Channel adoption, identity victory and collision satisfaction before `Established` cannot perform the reset."

Inference or gap: NONE

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: The plan's fate depends on the boundary rule. If a deadline equal to now counts as expired, the final guard discards the ordinary plan before any effects. The permit is not consumed and cannot be carried across an asynchronous boundary. No route revision, RIB change or ACK occurs. The missing timer input does not matter, because deadline validity is checked directly, not inferred from timer delivery. Room in numeric preflight does not authorize the commit either. The design does not say whether the coordinator must itself commit the expiry transition in this same serialized turn, or leave it to the timer owner. "Discarded or rebuilt" is the only instruction given.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Deadline validity is checked again at result application, not inferred from whether the timer callback has run."
QUOTE: "Expired/stale preparation is discarded or rebuilt before effects; the permit never crosses an asynchronous boundary"
QUOTE: "On expiry or terminal disposition, revoke authority first, cancel its timer, detach its effect target and request cooperative cancellation outside the executor; proceed with session cleanup without joining the provider."

Inference or gap: Missing rule: the design does not define whether a deadline equal to now is elapsed (inclusive or exclusive). Missing rule: no owner is named for advancing the session (committing the expiry/terminal transition) within the turn whose final guard observes expiry.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Disposal may update the normally stopped node's live cleanup accounting without reopening its lifecycle or subscriptions. Read-only queries do not themselves authorize canonical mutations or revision increments. Query capture time remains live rather than being frozen by ordinary stop; freezing is specified for numeric terminal capture. Disposal is the candidate canonical change that could advance revision, but the supplied document delegates exact revision costing to existing canonical-change/domain rules and does not state whether every cleanup-gauge-only change increments revision. That exact increment cannot be certified from this document alone.

Document support:

QUOTE: "Ordinary stopped instances remain queryable: later settlement may update cleanup gauges without reopening the lifecycle or event subscriptions."
QUOTE: "Ordinary stopped instances retain live accounting until an operational-domain terminal barrier actually occurs."
QUOTE: "OperationsStore validates the complete projection and exact numeric cost, using its existing domain rules and canonical-change classification"
QUOTE: "The current implementation's `#capture` samples wall time afresh even after terminal failure"

Inference or gap: Live capture time follows the ordinary/live versus numeric/frozen distinction and the stated baseline. Queries do not mutate by the scenario's premise. The precise revision consequence of a gauge-only disposal is missing because the referenced canonical-change classification is not reproduced.

--- ANSWER ---
Decision: Backoff expiry consumes only the timer; it cannot start a new attempt while required route capacity remains unavailable. Retain/register the one waiter and ended-attempt projection, with no retryAt after the timer expires. A release notification carries no reservation: if route capacity is full again at this adjacency's start check, no acquisition starts and waiting continues. Recompute blocked pools, including mandatory identity capacity. Preserve the remembered route-refusal set across these fluctuations; consume it only at actual next acquisition, or clear it on the other explicitly named satisfaction/terminal/stop transitions.

Document support:
